title: Three Springs and One Short Trowel
subtitle: 植物农业 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 植物农业（人与自然·自然生态·植物与农业）
meta: 主题语境：植物农业（人与自然·自然生态·植物与农业）　|　核心词汇：root　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 root 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1994 the gardener ① dug the root that no apprentice in the garden would have measured, and he said the digging was the whole of the spring. The ② root, meaning the base itself and not the trowel, ran three springs and stayed unmeasured in the book; a root, he said, is the only thing in a garden that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ root in that garden had the same short trowel beside it, and the ④ root at the far bed, meaning the cutting they kept for the children to plant and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A root, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to measure; the gardener said the measuring is the part that fills three springs.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the root was the whole of the matter, meaning the origin and not the base. The ⑥ root, meaning the origin and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody measures; root, he said, is either something you dig or the only word that means both a base and an origin. He said the origin is the part they remember.

By 1999 the ⑦ root had become a line in a notebook, and the notebook had become an argument about the short trowel. The ⑧ root of the whole thing, the gardener wrote in April, was one garden and three springs of measuring; root, he said, is either the cutting at the far bed or the reason you learned to measure. He said the measuring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ root I remember is the base measured in the notebook, which closed in 2001 and is still measured as the quietest in the garden. A ⑩ root, my mother said in 2003, is the only base that improves by being measured; every root, she said, is an origin that has agreed to look like a base. She said the origin was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 根；根源（指园子里每一条旁边的那一条）
B. n. 根；根源（指那条根本身，与小小的花铲相对）
C. 固定搭配：dig the root 挖这一条根
D. n. 根；根源（指留给孩子们插的那一枝）
E. n. 根之事（抽象总称，指一处园子的根之事）
F. n. 根；根源（指园艺笔记里写到、被测量的那一条）
G. n. 根、来处（指一件事里人人都种却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 来处（抽象总称，指人人都种却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: dug the root that no apprentice in the garden would have measured
The root, meaning the base itself and not the trowel
the root at the far bed
the root was the whole of the matter
the root had become a line in a notebook
The root of the whole thing
A root, my mother said in 2003

answers.why: dig the root 意为“挖这一条根”，1994 年那位园丁把园子里没有一位学徒肯测量的一条根做了一遍。
root 意为“根；根源”，指那条根本身而不是小小的花铲，它经过了三个春天而在簿子上没有被测量。
root 意为“根；根源”，指园子里每一条旁边的那一条，每一条旁边都有同一把小小的花铲。
root 意为“根；根源”，指最远那畦苗床的留给孩子们插的那一枝，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
root 意为“根、来处”，指一件事里人人都种却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这条来处就是那件事的全部。
root 意为“来处”，指人人都种却无人提起的那样东西而不是那条根，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
root 意为“根；根源”，指园艺笔记里写到、被测量的那一条，到 1999 年这一条成了园艺笔记里的一行。
root 意为“根之事”，园丁四月写道，整件事的根之事是一处园子和三个春天的测量。
root 意为“根；根源”，我记得的是园艺笔记里测量过的那一条，2001 年栽完了，至今仍被说成园子里最安静的一条。
root 为抽象总称，母亲 2003 年说，根是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的根。
